title: Server-Side Request Forgery at URL-fetch boundaries
summary: SSRF becomes plausible when attacker-influenced URL, host, scheme, redirect, or resolver state reaches a server-side network client. Verification must establish the real parser and resolution path, the reachable destination class, the server identity or network privilege used, and a bounded impact rather than assuming every URL-fetch feature is exploitable.
detection_signals: Untrusted URL or hostname data reaches an HTTP client, webhook tester, image fetcher, document renderer, import feature, proxy, or callback validator.
Validation and request execution use different parsers, canonicalization rules, DNS resolutions, redirect policies, or proxy settings.
The request path can reach loopback, link-local, private, internal service-discovery, cloud metadata, or attacker-controlled redirect destinations.
safe_local_tests: Use an isolated local listener and fixture hostname to prove whether the application performs the request without contacting third-party or production systems.
Exercise redirect, alternate-address, and re-resolution behavior only inside a controlled network namespace with explicit destination assertions.
Record the exact normalized URL, resolved address, redirect chain, request identity, response handling, and deny decision as regression evidence.
false_positive_traps: A URL parameter alone is not proof when a fixed allowlist, egress proxy, network policy, or post-resolution address check blocks unsafe destinations.
A static code path may be unreachable for the attacker's role, disabled configuration, required state, or production network boundary.
Blocking only literal localhost is not a complete control, but bypass speculation is not verification without evidence from the real parser and resolver path.
remediation_patterns: Prefer identifier-to-destination mappings over arbitrary URLs and enforce an allowlist for schemes, hosts, ports, paths, and redirect destinations.
Canonicalize once, resolve, reject non-public or otherwise forbidden address ranges, connect to the validated destination, and repeat checks after every redirect or re-resolution.
Combine application validation with least-privilege egress controls and isolate metadata, control-plane, and internal administrative services.
regression_proof: A local test proves the previously reachable forbidden fixture is blocked before a network connection while an explicitly allowed destination still works.
Tests cover parser ambiguity, redirects, resolution changes, IPv4 and IPv6 representations, and fail-closed behavior when validation or resolution is uncertain.
